title: Scheduled Agents, Dreaming and Q&A: Claude Managed Agents (Part 3 of 4) — Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic demos Claude Managed Agents: scheduled 'deployments' that spin up sessions on a cron with attached memory stores, plus a 'dreaming' preview that mines the last 30 days of session transcripts with sub-agents to find gaps and rewrite memory/skills. The Q&A is mostly product/API questions, but a few mechanisms (transcript-mining self-improvement, outcome rubrics with max iterations, eval-gated changes, letting the model choose sub-agent topology) are copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Periodically spin up sub-agents to read the last N days of session transcripts against a memory store, ask whether memory encoded what was needed, whether sessions hit issues, whether it recurred, then rewrite the memory/skill text.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it found that the skill that we created actually had a few gaps ... and it updated the memory store

takeaways.what_they_do: They insist the only way to know a change (including dreaming output) helped is running evals on representative tasks before adopting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything kind of ties back to eval. So like that that's how you would know whether something is performing
takeaways.numbers: claims customers saw 'significant improvement' on evals after dreaming, no figures

takeaways.technique: Outcome rubric + max iterations instead of fixed topology
takeaways.what_they_do: Define an exact outcome rubric and a max-iteration cap; the agent loops until it meets the rubric, and they avoid hard-coding sub-agent graphs, letting the model pick topology.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can define max iterations and the agent will keep going into it until it gets you that outcome

takeaways.what_they_do: They run compaction automatically so sessions can run for days without blowing the persistent store.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We we are running compaction for you so that you can run these for days. We've seen 10-hour sessions

takeaways.what_they_do: Emit every event (model call start/finish, etc.) via API and let consumers filter; don't pre-select what to observe.
takeaways.evidence_quote: right now you get all the events and you just filter them on your end

takeaways.technique: Scheduled deployments as recurring work primitive
takeaways.what_they_do: A deployment = agent definition + cron schedule + initial messages + attached resources (memory, repos, files), creating a fresh session each run.
